label: Route
description: An HTTP endpoint: each call to its path (and method) starts a fresh run carrying the request. The fixed ports carry method, path, captures, query and headers; the body arrives on the ports you declare on the arrow (`-> (user_id: String)`), one per top-level key, with no port for the whole body. A declared port named like a path capture reads the capture; one declared as a file kind (`photo: Image`) takes a `data:` URL or base64 and receives the stored file. Answer with Reply, Stream or Close downstream.

inputs.name: path
inputs.label: Path
inputs.description: Path under the project's live URL: literal segments and `{name}` captures (`users/{id}`), or empty for the root address. No leading '/'. Two routes may overlap only when one is strictly more specific (`cards/count` beside `cards/{id}`); otherwise activation refuses the pair.

inputs.name: method
inputs.label: Method
inputs.description: HTTP method served. Empty serves every method; another method on a served path gets 405.

inputs.name: dataType
inputs.label: Body shape
inputs.description: Body shape. `json`: top-level keys land on declared ports; a non-object body is refused. `text`: the whole body is a String on the one declared port. `bytes`: the body is stored and its stored-file value lands on the one declared port (declare `File`, or `Image`, which is checked against the bytes). Capture-named ports never count as that one port. Reply and Stream answer in this shape unless their `answerAs` says otherwise.

inputs.name: auth
inputs.description: Auth access node (ApiKeyAuth, JwtAuth, HmacAuth). Unwired, anyone with the URL may call. The established identity comes out on `caller`.

inputs.name: outlivesCaller
inputs.label: May outlive the caller
inputs.description: Off (default): the caller leaving cancels the run, and a long durable wait is killed instead of parked. On: the run is its own (answer early, keep working), so whatever runs after the answer must end by itself; anything that watches or loops needs `maxSessionSecs` or a TagRun/StopTagged pair.

inputs.name: defaultHoldSecs
inputs.label: Hold seconds before giving up on a wait
inputs.description: Caller-tied run only: how long a node's wait holds the worker (and the connection) before giving up. Per-wait overrides win. Never unbounded.

inputs.name: maxSessionSecs
inputs.label: Give up on one connection after this long
inputs.description: Hard ceiling on one connection, no default: it cuts a healthy feed on the clock. Only for an `outlivesCaller` run that has nothing else ending it (TagRun/StopTagged is usually better).

inputs.name: callerSilenceSecs
inputs.label: Call the caller gone after this much silence
inputs.description: Seconds the caller's machine may leave sent data unacknowledged before the caller counts as gone. Bounds silence, not call length: a present caller acks automatically, so hours-long feeds are untouched. Raise for clients whose link sleeps. `0` uses the OS default (about fifteen minutes).

inputs.name: maxInboundMb
inputs.label: Largest request body, in MB
inputs.description: Largest request body in MB; bigger is answered 413. A `data:` URL inflates its bytes by about a third, so the default 16 fits roughly 12 MB of picture.

inputs.name: journalEphemeral
inputs.label: Keep the exchange out of the journal
inputs.description: On: the journal keeps only sizes and counts, never the request or answer content (also hidden from you when debugging). Off (default): both are recorded, trimmed above 100 KB; raw bytes are never recorded.

inputs.name: recorded
inputs.label: Record each run
inputs.description: Off: a successful or cancelled run leaves nothing in `weft executions` but its cost; a failed one is still written down whole. For cheap, frequently polled routes. An unrecorded run cannot wait (timer, form), cannot outlive its caller, and is lost if the worker dies.

outputs.name: fired
outputs.description: Always true on a call; gate work on "the route was called".

outputs.name: method
outputs.description: The HTTP method the caller used.

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: Path as called, no leading slash (`users/42`).

outputs.name: caller
outputs.description: What the auth gate established: JWT claims, `{"key": <index>}` for an API key, `{}` for HMAC. Null with no `auth`.

then.message: Route '{id}' path starts with '/'. The gateway prefixes the route automatically; drop the leading slash.

Route '{id}' starts a run that never answers its caller: no node that answers it (a Reply, a Stream, a Close) is in it. Wire the answering node so the run reaches it (through data, or `_should_flow` on the node or on the group it sits in).

Route '{id}' would exist once per instance, because {per_instance_reason}, but its public address is one for every instance. Keep the route shared and pick the instance per call: the `Weft-Instance` header on a route gated by a connection, or an instance token.
